conversations.title: Find the action before adding another button
conversations.setting: Fictional discovery discussion using the lesson case: a stakeholder requests a button, while support notes describe difficulty finding an existing action.
turns: Sales stakeholder
Could you add a new export button to the home screen in the next release?
Product manager
Which user need would it address? Support notes mention difficulty finding the existing export action.
Sales stakeholder
Customers ask our team where to download their records. I assumed another button would solve that.
Product manager
That suggests a discoverability problem, but we haven't established the best solution or affected persona yet.
Sales stakeholder
Could we look at the support examples before deciding where any new control belongs?
Product manager
Yes. Let's clarify who was trying to export, from which page, and for what use case.
Sales stakeholder
I don't have those details here. I'll bring the original notes rather than invent a typical customer.
Product manager
Good. We should also consider opportunity cost before committing development capacity to a proposed solution.
Sales stakeholder
I'll describe the request as an export-discovery question, not an approved home-screen feature.
Product manager
Then we can investigate the problem and compare possible responses with the evidence in view.

conversations.title: Who needs the weekly digest?
conversations.setting: Fictional discovery interview: a department lead requests a weekly email digest but has not identified recipients or decisions it should support.
turns: Department lead
Our product needs a weekly email digest. Can that go straight into the backlog?
Product researcher
What decision would recipients make from it, and which people would actually receive the message?
Department lead
I had managers in mind, but I haven't asked whether they need weekly summaries.
Product researcher
Then the recipient persona and frequency are assumptions. Could we explore the underlying reporting task first?
Department lead
Managers sometimes ask for project updates. I don't know whether email is their preferred channel.
Product researcher
That's useful context, not confirmation of a digest use case. Can we speak with those managers?
Department lead
Yes. I'll introduce you and avoid promising a feature before we understand their workflow.
Product researcher
I'll ask what they currently review, what is missing, and what happens when information arrives late.
Department lead
Can the discovery conversation also reveal whether an existing view already meets part of the need?
Product researcher
Absolutely. That helps us compare options and avoid spending capacity before the problem is clear.

conversations.title: A competitor feature is not a user problem
conversations.setting: Fictional roadmap intake: a stakeholder asks for color-coded folders because a competitor offers them; no customer use case has been established.
turns: Marketing lead
A competitor has color-coded folders. Should we match that feature before our next announcement?
Product manager
What user problem would colors solve in our product, beyond making the feature lists look similar?
Marketing lead
Possibly faster organization, but that's my interpretation rather than something customers have told us.
Product manager
Then let's keep it as a hypothesis and identify a concrete organization task to investigate.
Marketing lead
Could we ask people who manage many folders how they currently find the right one?
Product manager
Yes. We should learn their use case and constraints without leading them toward colors as the answer.
Marketing lead
I can help recruit relevant users, although we haven't defined that persona precisely yet.
Product manager
Let's define the recruitment criteria together and consider the opportunity cost of any proposed build.
Marketing lead
I'll hold the launch claim until we have a problem statement and a prioritization decision.
Product manager
Good. Competitive information can prompt a question without dictating the solution we eventually choose.

additional_scenario.title: Why do users ask for printing?
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional support queue contains four requests for a print button. The records do not explain whether users need paper copies, portable files, or approval evidence. Clarify the use case before proposing a feature.
additional_scenario.role_a: Product manager: ask what task sits behind the request.
additional_scenario.role_b: Support lead: explain the limited evidence and offer to follow up with the requesters.
additional_scenario.opening_line: We have four requests for printing, but we haven't established what users need the output for.
additional_scenario.complication: A stakeholder says four identical feature requests prove one identical need.
success_checks: Separate requested solution from underlying need.
Identify missing audience and task information.
Agree a focused follow-up without promising implementation.

conversations.title: Three priorities, capacity for two
conversations.setting: Separate fictional roadmap case: saved filters, bulk export, and team templates each require four team-weeks. Eight team-weeks are available this quarter. Engineering has also assessed a personal-template slice at two team-weeks. Later capacity and stakeholder approval are unconfirmed.
turns: Portfolio sponsor
Saved filters, bulk export, and team templates are all urgent. Can we deliver all three?
Product manager
They total twelve team-weeks, but this quarter has eight. We need a scope or timing tradeoff.
Portfolio sponsor
Give me two concrete options rather than another request to prioritize everything.
Product manager
Option one: filters and export this quarter, if sponsors agree; propose team templates for a later confirmed slot.
Portfolio sponsor
And an option that gives template users something sooner, even with a narrower scope?
Product manager
Option two: filters plus the assessed personal-template slice, if accepted; defer export and shared templates.
Portfolio sponsor
That uses six weeks. Could the remaining two finish bulk export as well?
Product manager
No, export requires four. Spare capacity doesn't complete that feature; later delivery still needs confirmation.
Portfolio sponsor
I prefer option two, subject to template users accepting personal scope and the export sponsor agreeing.
Product manager
I'll seek those decisions before changing the roadmap; later dates remain uncommitted.

conversations.title: A dependency changes the order, not the goal
conversations.setting: Fictional planning: a new reporting view depends on an account-permissions update; both are proposed for the same planning period.
turns: Business sponsor
The reporting view is more visible. Can we build it before the account-permissions update?
Product manager
The proposed view depends on that update. Reversing the order may leave the view unable to work.
Business sponsor
Could the team start the visual design while the permissions dependency is being addressed?
Product manager
That may be possible, but parallel preparation isn't the same as completing the dependent feature first.
Business sponsor
Please show that distinction in the roadmap so stakeholders don't mistake an early mockup for delivery.
Product manager
Agreed. I'll ask the engineering lead which tasks can overlap and which require the dependency.
Business sponsor
If overlap isn't feasible, could we move the reporting commitment rather than pretend capacity increased?
Product manager
Yes. We'll compare that timing option with any reviewed scope reduction that still provides user value.
Business sponsor
I can support a conditional plan, provided the dependency and expected decision point are clear.
Product manager
I'll bring the assessed sequence before we convert the proposal into a delivery commitment.

conversations.title: Urgent intake after the roadmap is agreed
conversations.setting: Fictional product planning: a new sponsor requests a bulk-edit feature after the team has committed its available capacity; no estimate exists.
turns: Operations sponsor
We need bulk editing urgently. Can you add it to the already agreed roadmap?
Product manager
We can assess the request, but current capacity is committed and we have no estimate yet.
Operations sponsor
Could we call it a small enhancement so it doesn't displace anything already promised?
Product manager
The label doesn't establish effort. We need to understand the use case, dependencies, and testing scope.
Operations sponsor
Then what can we negotiate now before the estimate is available from engineering?
Product manager
We can clarify urgency and identify which existing outcome you would consider postponing if necessary.
Operations sponsor
I can discuss priorities, but I cannot approve moving another sponsor's committed work alone.
Product manager
I'll bring both sponsors into that tradeoff discussion once we have an assessed option.
Operations sponsor
Please acknowledge the request without telling users that bulk editing has a confirmed delivery date.
Product manager
Agreed. The roadmap changes only after the relevant scope, capacity, and approval questions are resolved.

additional_scenario.title: A smaller pilot instead of a full rollout
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional product team can assess a pilot for one department or a full rollout to four. Estimates and support needs are not yet known. A sponsor wants all four immediately. Negotiate the information and conditions needed for a smaller option.
additional_scenario.role_a: Product manager: offer a pilot assessment without guaranteeing its delivery date.
additional_scenario.role_b: Sponsor: explain the desired reach and consider a bounded first step.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Could we assess a one-department pilot while we clarify the capacity and support needs for all four?
additional_scenario.complication: The sponsor wants the pilot labeled a complete rollout on the roadmap.
success_checks: Distinguish pilot scope from full rollout.
Keep estimates and capacity unconfirmed.
Agree the evidence needed for prioritization.

conversations.title: Make quickly testable
conversations.setting: Fictional refinement using the lesson case: a user story says a page should load quickly without defining a measurable completion condition.
turns: Quality engineer
The user story says quickly. Could you specify what timing and conditions would count as acceptable?
Product manager
I haven't agreed a threshold yet. We should clarify the user expectation before choosing a number.
Quality engineer
Please include where timing starts and ends, plus the representative data and device conditions.
Product manager
That will help us avoid a test that passes only because it measures a different interaction.
Quality engineer
Exactly. Can we review proposed acceptance criteria before the team commits to the story?
Product manager
Yes. I'll bring the user context and ask engineering for feasible measurement conditions at refinement.
Quality engineer
Should the definition of done replace those story-specific criteria if it already requires testing?
Product manager
No. The shared completion checklist doesn't define what quickly means for this particular page.
Quality engineer
I'll keep the timing criterion open and identify empty and large-data cases for discussion.
Product manager
Good. We can agree a testable boundary without inventing a performance promise today.

conversations.title: What should happen when there are no results?
conversations.setting: Fictional search-story review: the story describes displaying matching records but says nothing about a search with zero matches.
turns: Frontend developer
The story covers matching records. What should users see when the search returns no results?
Product owner
That edge case isn't defined. We need a deliberate empty-state behavior rather than an accidental blank panel.
Frontend developer
Could you clarify whether the search term stays visible so users can revise it?
Product owner
I propose keeping it visible, but let's confirm the interaction with design before treating that as approved.
Frontend developer
Please bring the proposed behavior to tomorrow's refinement so I can estimate the complete story.
Product owner
I'll include the no-results case in the acceptance-criteria discussion and ask quality to review it.
Frontend developer
Should an unavailable search service show the same empty state because both return no displayed records?
Product owner
No, those are distinct situations to specify. Missing matches shouldn't be confused with a failed search.
Frontend developer
I'll identify both cases and leave their final behavior pending the refinement decision.
Product owner
Then we'll have explicit criteria instead of discovering the missing distinction during acceptance testing.

conversations.title: Saved locally or shared with the team?
conversations.setting: Fictional story discussion: a requirement says save the filter, but does not specify whether it belongs to one user or the whole team.
turns: Backend developer
When this story says save the filter, whose future sessions should use that saved setting?
Product owner
I intended a personal filter, but the story doesn't make that ownership clear.
Backend developer
Please confirm whether personal means this device only or the user's account across devices.
Product owner
That remains undecided. I'll ask the product designer to clarify the intended use case with me.
Backend developer
Could we resolve it before estimation? The persistence and access expectations affect the implementation scope.
Product owner
Yes. I'll request that decision at refinement and include the resulting acceptance criteria.
Backend developer
We should also discuss the edge case where a saved filter refers to a removed category.
Product owner
Agreed. Let's define that behavior explicitly instead of assuming the general definition of done covers it.
Backend developer
I'll bring the technical questions, but I won't silently choose account-wide storage as the product requirement.
Product owner
Thank you. We'll close refinement with the ownership boundary and any remaining decision clearly recorded.

additional_scenario.title: Cancel after an upload starts
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional upload story includes a Cancel control, but its behavior after transfer begins is undefined. No cancellation semantics have been approved. Request a bounded acceptance-criteria discussion covering user feedback and the saved-item state.
additional_scenario.role_a: Quality engineer: ask what cancellation should mean at this stage.
additional_scenario.role_b: Product owner: identify the decision needed and coordinate with engineering.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Could we define what Cancel does after transfer starts, including what the user sees afterward?
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague says any disappearance of the progress bar should count as success.
success_checks: Distinguish visual feedback from actual item state.
Request clear conditions before testing.
Agree a review owner and realistic discussion point.

conversations.title: More sign-ups, fewer completed setups
conversations.setting: Fictional analytics discussion using the lesson case: sign-ups increased but fewer users completed setup; a stakeholder calls the campaign a complete success.
turns: Marketing stakeholder
Sign-ups increased, so I called the acquisition campaign a complete product success in the update.
Product analyst
Sign-ups improved, but fewer users completed setup. Those stages tell us different things.
Marketing stakeholder
Could you explain activation without implying every sign-up should be counted as an active user?
Product analyst
Here activation is reaching the defined setup milestone. Signing up enters the funnel but doesn't complete it.
Marketing stakeholder
Then acquisition performance can improve while the next stage still raises a concern.
Product analyst
Exactly. We should inspect consistent cohorts and definitions before attributing the setup change to the campaign.
Marketing stakeholder
Does this evidence tell us whether those users will stay, or is retention another question?
Product analyst
Retention is another question about continued use over time, not established by this setup count.
Marketing stakeholder
I'll narrow the success claim to sign-ups and make the setup issue visible.
Product analyst
I'll bring the funnel breakdown and any comparability gaps before we recommend a response.

conversations.title: A returning visit is not the defined retention event
conversations.setting: Fictional product dashboard: retention is defined as completing a project task in a later week, but a draft counts any returning page view.
turns: Product manager
The draft retention chart counts returning page views. Is that our agreed retained-user definition?
Product analyst
No. Our current definition requires completing a project task in a later week.
Product manager
Then a visit and a retained user are not interchangeable measures for this report.
Product analyst
Correct. A returning visit shows activity, but it doesn't establish the task-based milestone we agreed.
Product manager
Could you explain that distinction on the chart without suggesting page views have no analytical value?
Product analyst
I'll label them as visits and calculate retention separately using the defined event and cohort.
Product manager
Do we know whether the required completion events are available for every week in the comparison?
Product analyst
That coverage still needs checking. I'll flag missing periods rather than count them as zero retention.
Product manager
Good. Keep the metric definition and observation window visible when you bring the revised view.
Product analyst
Then readers can distinguish engagement activity from the specific retention measure we actually use.

conversations.title: A younger cohort has had less time
conversations.setting: Fictional funnel review: an older sign-up cohort has seven days of setup observation; a newer cohort has only two days.
turns: Growth manager
The newer cohort has fewer completed setups. Does that prove the new onboarding flow performs worse?
Product analyst
Not yet. The older cohort has seven observation days, while the newer one has only two.
Growth manager
So we are comparing different opportunities to reach activation, not simply different interface versions.
Product analyst
Exactly. A cohort groups users by a shared starting event, but the observation window still matters.
Growth manager
Could you compare both cohorts at day two instead of waiting another five days?
Product analyst
That could provide an early matched view if the required event history is available.
Growth manager
And a day-two comparison wouldn't establish the seven-day result or long-term retention.
Product analyst
Correct. We should label the chosen window and keep later outcomes separate.
Growth manager
I'll remove the immediate failure claim and ask for the matched early funnel view.
Product analyst
I'll check event coverage and bring the comparison with its timing boundary clearly stated.

additional_scenario.title: One user makes five accounts
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional sign-up dashboard counts accounts, while an activation report counts unique people. One test participant created five accounts. The extent of multiple accounts elsewhere is unknown. Explain why the two measures cannot be treated as the same unit.
additional_scenario.role_a: Product analyst: explain accounts versus people.
additional_scenario.role_b: Growth lead: ask what definition and reconciliation are needed.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The sign-up figure counts accounts, but the activation report counts people, so their units differ.
additional_scenario.complication: The growth lead proposes dividing every account total by five.
success_checks: Distinguish the counting units.
Avoid generalizing from one participant.
Agree a consistent definition before comparing funnel stages.

conversations.title: One day of lift is not a completed test
conversations.setting: Fictional A/B-test review using the lesson case: one version has higher conversion after one day, before the planned duration ends.
turns: Growth lead
Version B has higher conversion after one day. Can we end the A/B test and launch it?
Experiment analyst
The planned duration hasn't elapsed. The observed difference isn't yet the completed readout we agreed to use.
Growth lead
Are you saying the higher rate is false, or that our conclusion should stay provisional?
Experiment analyst
The observed rate stands. The interpretation needs the planned analysis, including uncertainty and guardrail metrics.
Growth lead
Could statistical significance alone settle the rollout decision if a dashboard happens to display it today?
Experiment analyst
It wouldn't replace the decision plan or review of practical effects and possible harms.
Growth lead
Then I'll report early directional results without describing the hypothesis as confirmed.
Experiment analyst
Good. We'll continue following the agreed monitoring and decision process, including any established safety escalation.
Growth lead
Please tell me what is observed now and what remains pending at the next check-in.
Experiment analyst
I'll bring those separately so one encouraging day doesn't become an unsupported product conclusion.

conversations.title: Conversion improves while support contacts rise
conversations.setting: Fictional experiment readout: the treatment shows higher conversion and more support contacts; uncertainty and the prespecified guardrail evaluation are pending.
turns: Product manager
The treatment converts more users. Can our recommendation focus on that improvement alone?
Experiment owner
Support contacts also increased, and the guardrail evaluation is pending. That belongs in the same discussion.
Product manager
Does the increase prove users were confused by the treatment, or is that an interpretation?
Experiment owner
It is an interpretation. We observed more contacts, but haven't established their cause or composition.
Product manager
Then please separate the contact count from the hypothesis about confusion in the readout.
Experiment owner
I will. We'll also assess uncertainty and the predefined guardrail rather than invent a threshold afterward.
Product manager
Could a conversion gain still be practically unattractive if support workload rises enough?
Experiment owner
Potentially. That tradeoff needs the actual evidence and agreed decision criteria, not just one favorable metric.
Product manager
I'll leave the rollout recommendation open until that combined assessment is available.
Experiment owner
I'll bring the benefit, guardrail result, and unresolved attribution questions together for review.

conversations.title: The test changed two things at once
conversations.setting: Fictional product experiment: version B changes both a headline and button placement; the observed conversion rate is higher than version A.
turns: Designer
Version B converted more users, so the new headline must be the reason.
Experiment analyst
B also moved the button. The comparison doesn't isolate the headline from that layout change.
Designer
Then our hypothesis about the headline alone isn't directly tested by this combined treatment.
Experiment analyst
Correct. We can discuss the observed combination while keeping individual-component explanations unconfirmed.
Designer
Would a statistically significant combined effect prove that both changes helped independently?
Experiment analyst
No. It would not establish each component's contribution or rule out interactions between them.
Designer
I'll describe B as the combined version and remove the headline-only claim from the review.
Experiment analyst
Please keep the exact treatment description with the result so future readers know what changed.
Designer
If we need the individual contribution, we'll propose a separate experiment rather than rewrite this one's history.
Experiment analyst
Agreed. First complete the planned readout, including guardrails, before deciding what further question to test.

additional_scenario.title: The slide and dashboard disagree on the treatment label
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional test dashboard identifies the treatment as B, but a draft slide calls A the treatment. No published readout has been sent. Discuss how to verify assignments and correct the presentation before interpreting results.
additional_scenario.role_a: Experiment analyst: request the assignment record and treatment definition.
additional_scenario.role_b: Product manager: pause the conclusion and confirm the correction route.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The slide and dashboard disagree about the treatment label, so we need to verify assignment before interpreting the result.
additional_scenario.complication: A stakeholder says the larger number can simply be labeled the winner.
success_checks: Verify labels from the source record.
Do not select a treatment identity from outcome size.
Agree a corrected readout with uncertainty and guardrails retained.

conversations.title: Support has not received the migration notes
conversations.setting: Fictional release handoff using the lesson case: a release is ready for review, but required migration notes have not reached support.
turns: Release manager
The release is ready for review. Have you received the migration notes required by our checklist?
Support lead
No. We have the feature summary, but not the instructions explaining the customer migration changes.
Release manager
Then support enablement remains incomplete. I shouldn't describe the overall launch handoff as finished.
Support lead
Please identify the migration-note owner and the version we should review when it arrives.
Release manager
I'll contact the owner and request the reviewed notes through our release channel.
Support lead
Does receiving the file mean we have accepted the handoff, or should we confirm understanding too?
Release manager
Please confirm you can access it and raise any unresolved support questions before readiness is assessed.
Support lead
We also need the relevant rollback information identified, not assumed from an older release.
Release manager
I'll include that request and keep launch readiness pending the required checklist review.
Support lead
Understood. We'll acknowledge the actual materials received and make any remaining enablement gaps explicit.

conversations.title: A rollback link points to the previous release
conversations.setting: Fictional release preparation: the current checklist links to a previous release's rollback notes; applicability has not been checked.
turns: Support engineer
The rollback link opens last month's notes. Are those instructions confirmed for this release?
Release coordinator
Not yet. I'll ask the release owner to verify applicability rather than assume the link is sufficient.
Support engineer
Please include the correct release identifier in the handoff so we can distinguish the versions.
Release coordinator
Agreed. The current package is awaiting that check, even though the link itself opens successfully.
Support engineer
Can I mark documentation accessible while keeping rollback readiness pending in our acceptance response?
Release coordinator
Yes. Those are separate checks, and your acknowledgment should preserve that distinction.
Support engineer
Who should receive questions if the verified notes describe a customer migration that support hasn't practiced?
Release coordinator
I'll identify the migration owner and arrange a readiness discussion before the handoff is considered complete.
Support engineer
I'll confirm receipt of the corrected package and repeat any constraints in our response.
Release coordinator
Thank you. A working link won't be treated as evidence that the receiving team has applicable guidance.

conversations.title: Feature enabled is not customer migration complete
conversations.setting: Fictional staged launch: a feature flag is enabled for a pilot group, while migration confirmation from that group is pending.
turns: Product manager
The pilot feature flag is enabled. Can support tell the pilot customers their migration is complete?
Release engineer
Not yet. Enabling access and confirming each customer's migration are separate steps in this launch.
Product manager
What should the receiving support team be able to confirm from your handoff today?
Release engineer
The pilot scope, enabled configuration, and the fact that migration confirmation remains pending.
Product manager
Please make clear that the feature isn't enabled for every customer in the wider release audience.
Release engineer
I will. I'll include the pilot boundary and point to the migration-status owner.
Product manager
Should support use the old rollout announcement as their customer response until a new one arrives?
Release engineer
Only reviewed, applicable communication should be used; the old announcement may describe a different scope.
Product manager
I'll coordinate the current wording and ask support to acknowledge the pilot limitation explicitly.
Release engineer
Then our handoff will distinguish enabled access, confirmed migration, and broader launch readiness accurately.

additional_scenario.title: The receiving team cannot access the demo
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional support-enablement session needs a demonstration environment. The release notes are available, but support accounts cannot enter the demo. No training has occurred. Give a handoff and agree the missing readiness check.
additional_scenario.role_a: Release coordinator: acknowledge the access gap and name the next owner request.
additional_scenario.role_b: Support lead: confirm received notes without claiming training completion.
additional_scenario.opening_line: We have the release notes, but demo access is blocked, so support practice has not happened yet.
additional_scenario.complication: A manager wants attendance at the scheduled session counted as completed enablement.
success_checks: Distinguish attendance, access, and completed practice.
Request an access update through the proper owner.
Confirm readiness remains pending the necessary handoff checks.

conversations.title: Fast workaround or a stronger interface
conversations.setting: Fictional platform discussion using the lesson case: a workaround could deliver sooner, while improving the underlying interface would take longer.
turns: Business sponsor
Can we choose the workaround since it delivers the requested feature sooner?
Product manager
We can compare it with the interface improvement, but speed shouldn't be our only criterion.
Business sponsor
What else belongs beside delivery time when explaining this tradeoff to nontechnical stakeholders?
Product manager
Maintenance effort, reliability evidence, affected users, and the cost of revisiting the workaround later.
Business sponsor
Is that what you mean by technical debt: work we may need to repay through future changes?
Product manager
Yes, broadly. Here we should describe the specific maintenance obligation rather than use the phrase as a warning.
Business sponsor
Do we have confirmed reliability results for both options, or are we comparing assumptions?
Product manager
Those results are not provided yet. We'll label estimates and request the engineering assessment.
Business sponsor
I'll consider a bounded workaround if its limits and follow-up ownership are explicit.
Product manager
I'll bring comparable options and conditions before asking you to choose a delivery approach.

conversations.title: One customer exception or a reusable API change
conversations.setting: Fictional platform planning: one customer requests an extra response field; the team can assess a customer-specific exception or a shared API change.
turns: Account manager
Could engineering add the field only for this customer so we avoid a platform discussion?
Platform product manager
That option needs comparison with a shared application programming interface, or API, change.
Account manager
Why consider a broader change when only one customer has asked for the field so far?
Platform product manager
A special case may add maintenance and testing obligations. A shared change may affect more consumers.
Account manager
So neither option is automatically better simply because its visible scope looks smaller or larger.
Platform product manager
Correct. Compare delivery effort, compatibility, reliability checks, and future support using the same criteria.
Account manager
Can you promise the exception now while the shared design is still being assessed?
Platform product manager
No. We haven't established its effort or safety for existing consumers, so timing remains unconfirmed.
Account manager
I'll tell the customer the request is under assessment and explain which tradeoff we are reviewing.
Platform product manager
I'll return with bounded options rather than make a platform commitment from an unreviewed exception.

conversations.title: A manual retry hides recurring maintenance work
conversations.setting: Fictional product operations: a failing import sometimes succeeds after a manual retry; the cause and frequency are not yet quantified.
turns: Operations lead
Manual retry often completes the import. Could we keep that workaround instead of prioritizing a fix?
Product manager
We should compare its ongoing support burden with the effort and expected benefit of investigating the interface.
Operations lead
We don't have a reliable failure frequency yet, so the burden is still an estimate.
Product manager
Then let's measure incidents and staff time before calling the workaround cheap or the fix unnecessary.
Operations lead
Would you label this technical debt even though the immediate customer task can eventually finish?
Product manager
The recurring manual obligation is the useful detail. The label alone doesn't establish priority or cause.
Operations lead
Can we keep reporting successful retries while making the unresolved reliability issue visible?
Product manager
Yes. Recovery success and first-attempt reliability answer different questions and should be tracked separately.
Operations lead
I'll bring a consistent record of failures, retries, and handling time to the next prioritization review.
Product manager
Then we can compare options on evidence instead of assuming hidden work costs nothing.

additional_scenario.title: Supporting two API versions
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional platform supports version 1, and a proposed version 2 would simplify a new feature. Existing customer migration effort is unknown. Compare maintaining both versions with a reviewed migration approach without announcing a retirement date.
additional_scenario.role_a: Platform product manager: outline common comparison criteria.
additional_scenario.role_b: Customer-success lead: raise unknown migration and support needs.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Version two may simplify the feature, but we haven't assessed what existing customers need to migrate.
additional_scenario.complication: A stakeholder says a newer version makes migration effort irrelevant.
success_checks: Compare delivery, maintenance, compatibility, and customer effort.
Keep migration assumptions explicit.
Avoid promising retirement or migration dates without assessment.

conversations.title: Agree a criterion before choosing a feature
conversations.setting: Fictional executive discussion using the lesson case: two executives favor different product options without a shared decision criterion.
turns: Product manager
We have competing preferences. Could we agree the decision criterion before selecting either product option?
Executive sponsor
One executive values expansion, while the other wants stronger retention. Neither has defined the priority.
Product manager
Let's invite both to explain strategic fit and the outcome each option is expected to support.
Executive sponsor
Would collecting their opinions again simply repeat the disagreement without moving us forward?
Product manager
We should ask for evidence and tradeoffs, then clarify who has the authority to decide.
Executive sponsor
I'll confirm the decision owner. We also need the support team's view of the operational impact.
Product manager
Agreed. Their perspective belongs in the discussion before any recommendation becomes a decision memo.
Executive sponsor
Can you summarize what is unresolved at the end rather than claim consensus from a quiet room?
Product manager
Yes: shared criterion, operational impact, and confirmed decision ownership remain the immediate questions.
Executive sponsor
I'll bring the relevant voices together so the next discussion can reach an accountable next step.

conversations.title: Revenue potential and onboarding effort
conversations.setting: Fictional product review: sales favors a specialist feature, while customer success questions onboarding effort; neither impact estimate is verified.
turns: Product director
Sales wants the specialist feature, but customer success has concerns. How should we frame this decision?
Product manager
Let's hear both views using the same criteria: expected customer value, onboarding effort, and strategic fit.
Product director
Sales has a revenue estimate. Does that settle the tradeoff before we hear support concerns?
Product manager
The estimate is unverified, and operational effort is also unverified. Neither should be treated as established.
Product director
Then invite the owners to explain their assumptions rather than argue over whose forecast sounds stronger.
Product manager
I'll do that and distinguish evidence, estimates, and unknowns in the decision discussion.
Product director
Who should decide whether this feature belongs ahead of the existing roadmap commitments?
Product manager
We should confirm that authority through our planning process instead of assuming this meeting can approve it.
Product director
Good. Close with the evidence needed and the decision owner, not an implied commitment to sales.
Product manager
I'll capture those next steps and preserve any remaining disagreement accurately in the decision memo.

conversations.title: A loud meeting does not equal stakeholder agreement
conversations.setting: Fictional product meeting: an executive strongly supports a redesign; the accessibility lead has not spoken and review findings remain unknown.
turns: Executive sponsor
The redesign has strong support in this room. Can we say stakeholders are aligned?
Product manager
We haven't heard from the accessibility lead, and their review findings aren't available yet.
Executive sponsor
Could we record alignment now and add their comments when they eventually arrive?
Product manager
That would imply agreement we haven't obtained. We can record the current preference and pending review separately.
Executive sponsor
Please invite their perspective, but keep the discussion focused on the decision we actually need.
Product manager
I'll ask which findings affect the proposed scope and what remains unassessed, without assuming their conclusion.
Executive sponsor
And how do we avoid turning every unresolved detail into an indefinite product delay?
Product manager
Confirm the decision owner and the evidence they need, then agree a review checkpoint.
Executive sponsor
That works. I'll help establish the decision route rather than ask you to manufacture consensus.
Product manager
I'll summarize support, pending input, and the next decision step as distinct parts of the executive narrative.

additional_scenario.title: A strategic-fit claim without a named objective
additional_scenario.brief: A fictional proposal is described as strategically essential, but the sponsor has not identified which current product objective it supports. The team has two competing proposals. Facilitate a short comparison and clarify the decision route.
additional_scenario.role_a: Product manager: ask for the objective and relevant evidence.
additional_scenario.role_b: Executive sponsor: explain the intended outcome while acknowledging the missing comparison.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Which product objective does this proposal support, and what criterion should we use to compare it with the alternative?
additional_scenario.complication: The sponsor asks you to omit the alternative from the decision discussion.
success_checks: Connect strategic fit to a named objective or an explicit gap.
Preserve the relevant competing perspective.
Agree criteria and decision ownership without implying approval.
